# MCP tool and prompt reference

<!-- GENERATED by `npm run docs` (mcp-server/scripts/gen-docs.ts) from mcp-server/src/tools.ts and src/prompts.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Server `terraria` 0.1.0. Every tool exactly as `tools/list` returns it: description (what the LLM reads), input schema and annotations; then every prompt as `prompts/get` returns it. Overview, events, errors and environment: [MCP.md](MCP.md).

Kinds: **read-only** observes and never needs control; **async task** starts a task and returns at once (follow with `wait_for_task`; it replaces a running task); **instant action** acts and returns the outcome. Every non-read-only tool except `request_control` fails with `user_has_control` while the user drives.

## Server instructions

Sent in the `initialize` result (`instructions`), verbatim:

```text
You control the user's own Terraria character through the LlmPlayer mod.
- Control: action tools need AI mode. Call request_control to switch it on yourself; the user can also hand control over with the toggle key (default Insert). The user pressing Insert takes control back at once and cancels the current task; after that request_control is refused until the user hands control over again — respect that, stop, and ask them. Dying cancels the current task but you keep control.
- Coordinates: absolute tile coordinates, y grows DOWNWARD (smaller y = higher up). The player's position (x,y) is the bottom-left tile of its 2-wide x 3-tall body (feet-left): it occupies x..x+1, y-2..y, standing on tile row y+1.
- Fair vision: you only see what the player could see. '?' in get_map = unknown/unrevealed tiles; find/get_entities only report visible things (exception: get_state lists every living boss, as the vanilla boss health bar does).
- Actions start asynchronous tasks and return immediately. Only one task runs at a time; starting a new one cancels the old. Follow an action with wait_for_task (blocks until done) or get_task (poll).
- Suggested loop: get_state -> get_map -> pick an action -> wait_for_task -> repeat. Check events in results (damage taken, control changes).
- Never breaks protected tiles (furniture, chests, doors, stations, NPC houses, spawn area), never attacks town NPCs/critters, never teleports or spawns items.
```

## Control

### get_control

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Who is driving the character: {driver: 'user'|'ai'}. Only 'ai' lets action tools work.

Parameters: none.

### request_control

Kind: **action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Switch AI mode on so action tools work: {driver, granted, reason?}. Refused (granted false, with the reason) after the user took control back with Insert — then only the user can hand it over again, so ask them — and while the player is dead.

Parameters: none.

## Observation

### get_state

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Player status: position {x,y}, life/mana/defense, buffs, held item, freeSlots (empty main inventory slots of 50; at 0 new items that don't stack are left on the ground), time of day, biome, depth layer, spawn point, driver, current task and recent events (damage, kills, pickups, deaths; drained by each get_state). Optional fields, present only when relevant: breath {now, max} (only while below max, i.e. the head has been under water/honey; at 0 you drown. A reflex surfaces for air on its own below 45% and resumes the task at 90%; routes avoid more than ~11 tiles under water unless you have gills), nearbyHostiles {count, nearest} (visible hostile NPCs within 40 tiles and the nearest one's distance), boss [{id, name, life, lifeMax, x?, y?, distance?, segments?}] (every boss alive in the world with its life, like the vanilla boss health bar; x/y/distance only while you can see it; segmented bosses merged), worldEvents (e.g. 'blood moon', 'goblin army', 'slime rain', 'rain'), openChest {x, y, name} (the container open right now; see open_chest), housing {homeless?: [names], canMoveIn?: [names]} (town NPCs without a house, and NPCs whose move-in conditions are met: they arrive during the day once a free valid house exists; see check_housing / build_house), lastDeaths [{text, killer, x, y, time, secondsAgo}] (the last 5 deaths in this world, newest first, never drained: what killed you and where). Start every decision here. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body.

Parameters: none.

### get_map

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

ASCII map centred on the player with a legend and the top-left corner's coordinates. '@' player, '#' solid, '.' air, '=' platform, '~' water, 'L' lava, 'T' tree, 'C' chest, 'W' crafting station, 'D' closed door (move_to opens and closes doors on its way), lowercase letters = ores (see legend), 'E' enemy, 'N' town NPC, 'i' dropped item, '?' unknown (not yet seen — may be anything). Row r, column c is tile (left+c, top+r). Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1, ≤ 40 |  | Half-width in tiles, default 20, max 40 |

### get_entities

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Visible NPCs, enemies, critters, dropped items and hostile projectiles near the player (max 30): {id, name, kind: hostile|town|critter|item|projectile, x, y, life, lifeMax, distance}, plus when relevant profession (town NPCs with a personal name: e.g. name 'Demetrius', profession 'Arms Dealer'), boss: true, vx/vy (velocity in tiles/second, omitted when still; +y = falling/downward), damage (contact or projectile damage) and defense (hostiles). Ordered bosses first (nearest 10 segments), then threats (hostile NPCs and up to 10 projectiles), then everything else, nearest first within each group. Use id with move_to/attack/talk_to_npc/buy (projectile ids are informational only; talk_to_npc and buy also take the name or profession).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1 |  | Search radius in tiles, default 40 |

### find

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Nearest visible things of a category (max 10, nearest first): ores, trees, chests (any container), crafting stations, beds, NPCs, dropped items, blocks by name (category block + name, e.g. 'Stone', 'Sand', 'Clay': get_map shows every solid tile as '#'), or valuable: cave loot and landmarks — 'Life Crystal' (collect it: +20 max life), 'Life Fruit', 'Pot' (collect: coins, potions, torches), chests by their in-game name ('Gold Chest', 'Locked Gold Chest' = dungeon, needs a key: refused), 'Enchanted Sword (in stone)' / 'Sword in Stone (maybe a decoy)' (collect), 'Demon Altar' / 'Crimson Altar' (crafting station for boss summons, e.g. Suspicious Looking Eye; can't be broken), 'Shadow Orb (don't break)' / 'Crimson Heart (don't break)' (breaking one has world effects; the third summons a boss — never broken by the AI) and 'Fallen Star' items on the ground; or plant: harvestable herbs and mushrooms ('Daybloom', 'Moonglow', 'Blinkroot', 'Deathweed', 'Waterleaf', 'Fireblossom', 'Shiverthorn', '… (blooming)' = also drops seeds, 'Mushroom', 'Vile Mushroom' (Vile Powder → Worm Food), 'Vicious Mushroom', 'Glowing Mushroom'): harvest one with mine at its x,y. Objects report their top-left tile. Only searches tiles the player has seen; explore / explore_caves to reveal more. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | `"ore" \| "tree" \| "chest" \| "station" \| "bed" \| "npc" \| "item" \| "block" \| "valuable" \| "plant"` | yes |  |  |  |
| `name` | `string` | no |  |  | Name filter, e.g. 'Copper Ore', 'Work Bench', 'Guide'; required for block ('Stone', 'Sand') |
| `radius` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1 |  | Search radius in tiles, default 60 |

### get_inventory

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Hotbar (slots 0-9), main inventory, armor, accessories, ammo, coins, the selected hotbar slot and freeSlots (empty slots of the 50 hotbar + main slots: at 0, picked-up items that don't stack onto a slot are left lying; free some with drop_item, trash: true for junk). Empty slots are omitted. Hotbar/inventory/ammo items carry tags only when true: weapon + damage (with your bonuses), heal (life restored), ammo, consumable (used up on use, e.g. potions), placeable (blocks, walls, furniture), pick/axe/hammer (tool power, axe as shown in game). For choosing attack's weapon and ammo: weapons also carry useTime (ticks per use, 60 = 1 s; lower = faster), ammoType (the ammo class they fire, e.g. "arrow", "bullet") and mana (cost per use); ammo stacks carry damage (added to the weapon's per shot) and ammoType. Each hit loses about half the target's defense (get_entities shows defense), so against armored enemies fewer, harder hits win.

Parameters: none.

## Tasks

### get_task

Kind: **read-only** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Current task and the last finished one: {current, lastFinished}, each {name, status: running|succeeded|failed|cancelled, reason, progress, result?} (result only for tasks that return data, e.g. talk_to_npc, attack, explore). Use wait_for_task to block instead of polling.

Parameters: none.

### wait_for_task

Kind: **read-only, blocks** · annotations: readOnlyHint=true

Block until the current task finishes (succeeded, failed or cancelled) or timeout_s passes (default 30, max 300). Returns {timed_out, report: {name, status, reason, progress, result?}}; result carries data from tasks like talk_to_npc and attack. If timed_out, the task is still running: call again, or cancel_task. Call this after every task-starting action.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout_s` | `number` | no | ≥ 0, ≤ 300 | `30` | Seconds to wait, default 30 |

### cancel_task

Kind: **instant action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Stop the running task; the player stops moving. Instant action (no task). Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

Parameters: none.

### wait

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Stand still for N seconds (max 60), with reflexes still active — e.g. to let night pass near shelter. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | `number` | yes | > 0, ≤ 60 |  |  |

## Movement and exploration

### move_to

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Walk to a tile or an entity with smart pathfinding (jumps, drops, platforms; digs and builds if allowed). Give x,y (a standing position; a target inside solid ground snaps to the nearest standable tile) or entity_id from get_entities. Fails with a reason if unreachable. Travel memory: the mod remembers where you have stood this session (a trail every ~8 tiles, per world, also your own walks when the user drives). A tile goal beyond one planning window (more than ~120 tiles across or ~80 up/down) first follows that trail toward the goal (surface trails preferred; progress says "following a known trail"), hop by hop, then plans the rest normally; a walk that stops making progress tries the trail instead of failing. So for long trips, walking a route once (e.g. along the surface via waypoints) makes later trips reliable. Torches (default on, needs torches in the inventory): in the dark underground or in a tunnel it digs, with no torch within ~10 tiles, it pauses between steps, places a torch within reach and walks on, so the way is revealed (the pathfinder only knows tiles you have seen: unlit tunnels stay unknown). Never in an NPC house or the spawn area. Platform reserve: building keeps platform_reserve platforms (default 20, see set_reflexes) for later descents: the route may only use platforms above it plus cheap blocks, bridges and climbs switch to dirt/stone/… at the reserve, and only when no route fits does it use the reserve (reserveReleased). When the task ends, report.result is {torchesPlaced, platformsUsed, blocksUsed, platformsLeft, reserveReleased, note?} (note when platforms run short). Water Walking (Water Walking Potion, or Water Walking Boots and their upgrades): lakes and honey are walked over like floor (lava too only with lava immunity); drink the potion first with use_item. With the potion the route never stops on the water and crossings longer than the buff time left are refused ("water walking would run out"): drink a fresh one. Without it a non-swimmer only crosses water along the bottom (within breath) or over a platform bridge. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |
| `entity_id` | `integer` | no |  |  | Entity id from get_entities, instead of x,y |
| `allow_dig` | `boolean` | no |  |  | May mine through blocks on the way, default true |
| `allow_build` | `boolean` | no |  |  | May place platforms/blocks to climb, bridge, or build down a drop too deep to fall safely (a platform below the feet, then drop onto it), default true |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Light the walk: place torches from the inventory in the dark (underground or in a dug tunnel, about every 10 tiles), default true |
| `platform_reserve` | `integer` | no | ≥ 0, ≤ 9999 |  | Platforms to keep for this walk unless no route fits without them (default: set_reflexes platform_reserve, 20) |

### explore

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Travel roughly `distance` tiles in a direction, revealing the map as it goes. Good for finding ores, trees and caves. Walks toward the farthest visible ground; when there is none (e.g. solid ground below or a wall ahead) and allow_dig is on, it digs with your best pickaxe: down = a 2-wide shaft under you (you drop as the floor goes; move_to climbs back out with platforms), left/right = a 3-tall tunnel. Digging up isn't supported. It only digs tiles it can see and stops with a reason before lava/water next to the hole, protected tiles, tiles too hard for the pickaxe ("needs pick power N at (x,y)") or an unsafe drop. Dark tiles: it places a torch from your inventory and looks again ("too dark: no torches" without any); with torches on it also lights dark spots underground about every 10 tiles. With Water Walking (potion via use_item first, or Water Walking Boots) a lake ahead counts as floor and is walked over (with the potion only when the far shore is in view and the buff lasts the crossing). surface (left/right): follow the ground's surface over hills and valleys instead of keeping the current height: each leg walks to the farthest visible surface point, then looks again; it never tunnels (stops with "no visible surface" when nothing ahead is known). Progress shows walking/digging; result: {covered, dug, torchesPlaced, stoppedBecause?}. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `"left" \| "right" \| "down" \| "up"` | yes |  |  |  |
| `distance` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1 |  | Tiles to cover, default 50 |
| `allow_dig` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Dig when there is no visible ground to walk to, default true |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Place torches from the inventory in the dark, default true |
| `surface` | `boolean` | no |  |  | left/right only: follow the visible ground surface up and down hills, never tunnel; default false |

### explore_caves

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Explore caves systematically through their open space, revealing the map, to find Life Crystals and other cave loot. Started in the surface layer it first goes underground (walks down, or digs a 2-wide shaft like explore down). Then it repeatedly walks to a known ledge next to the nearest reachable edge between known open space and unknown tiles (digging only through walls up to 3 tiles thick to reach the next cave), lights the dark opening with a torch from your inventory (also underground whenever it's dark and no torch is within ~10 tiles), looks, and moves on. A dark cave whose floor isn't known yet is lit from its edge first. When the cave pocket is exhausted it tunnels toward the nearest large unrevealed region (down preferred, else left/right): a 2-wide shaft or 3-tall tunnel of at most 40 tiles per tunnel (max 10 per area; an attempt that dug nothing — its start unreachable — doesn't count and another start is tried) through rock your pickaxe can break, never toward known lava, through water/honey, protected or too-hard tiles, never into an unsafe drop, torches in the dark; as soon as it breaks into open space it explores again (radius then counts from there). When the whole neighbourhood is exhausted (no opening, no short tunnel, or 6 walks in a row failed) it relocates: travels to the nearest large unexplored region on the map ('?' country, up to ~250 tiles left/right at the current depth or down), walking through known caves and tunnelling through rock with the same safety rules and torches, then explores there (max 4 relocations per call). Failed walks and tunnel starts are remembered across calls (per world, ~20 min), so the next call doesn't retry them. Avoids lava (never walks through it, skips openings within 3 tiles of it) and unsafe drops. Stops (succeeded) when something in stop_on that wasn't visible at the start comes into view — report.reason says what and where (a Life Crystal: 'found a Life Crystal at (x,y): collect it for +20 max life'), report.result.stoppedAt has it; each thing stops only one call (later calls just list it in found, for ~20 min), and rigged Dead Man's Chests and chests you opened before that are empty now never stop it — or when max_seconds is up or no reachable opening, no safe tunnel and no relocation is left (the reason says why each direction was refused); fails when walks keep failing and neither a tunnel nor a relocation is possible, or if it can't get underground. Kinds: life_crystal, life_fruit, pot, chest, enchanted_sword, altar, orb, ore, fallen_star (default stop_on: life_crystal, chest, enchanted_sword, life_fruit; [] = only time/radius). collect_pots: true breaks visible pots within 12 tiles on the way. Result: {revealedTiles (approximate), found: [{kind, name, x, y}] (everything newly seen, max 30), torchesPlaced, potsBroken, legs, descended (tiles dug getting underground), tunnels (that dug or moved), tunnelled (tiles dug in tunnels and relocations), failedTunnels (attempts that couldn't start), relocations, relocated (tiles travelled relocating), lifeCrystals: [{kind, name, x, y}] (every Life Crystal seen, also ones in view at the start), stoppedBecause, stoppedAt?}. Then: collect for life crystals/pots, loot_chest for chests, mine_vein for ore. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `integer` | no | ≥ 10, ≤ 200 |  | Max distance in tiles from the start (after a tunnel: from where it broke through), default 80 |
| `max_seconds` | `integer` | no | ≥ 5, ≤ 600 |  | Time limit, default 120 |
| `stop_on` | `"life_crystal" \| "life_fruit" \| "pot" \| "chest" \| "enchanted_sword" \| "altar" \| "orb" \| "ore" \| "fallen_star"[]` | no |  |  | Stop when one of these comes into view; default life_crystal, chest, enchanted_sword, life_fruit |
| `collect_pots` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Break pots seen on the way (within 12 tiles), default false |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Place torches in the dark, default true |

## Gathering and mining

### mine

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Mine one tile: walks within reach, picks the best pickaxe and digs it. Fails on protected tiles or if the pickaxe is too weak. To break a pot or life crystal and also pick up what drops, use collect. Inventory full: the reason ends with "inventory full: … not picked up" for drops that didn't fit. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Light the walk: place torches from the inventory in the dark (underground or in a dug tunnel, about every 10 tiles), default true |

### mine_area

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Mine every tile in the rectangle (x1,y1)-(x2,y2), inclusive, at most 200 tiles, top row first. Tiles that can't or mustn't be mined are skipped, not fatal: air, trees, hammer-only, protected, locked (holding up an object), not visible, too hard for your pickaxe. The reply (and the finished task's report.result) has skipped, skippedReasons {reason: count}, skippedTiles [{x,y,reason}] (first 10, air omitted) and torchesPlaced (walks are lit like move_to's). Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x1` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y1` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |
| `x2` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y2` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Light the walk: place torches from the inventory in the dark (underground or in a dug tunnel, about every 10 tiles), default true |

### mine_vein

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Mine one connected deposit: give any visible tile of it. Ore: the whole vein (every visible tile of the same ore connected to it, 8-neighbourhood, up to 200) by default. Any other block (Stone, Sand, Clay, Mud…): `max` tiles of it (default 20), nearest to the given tile first — e.g. 20 Stone for a furnace. Only that block type is mined, not what surrounds it. Tiles it can't reach or break are skipped and reported (report.result.skippedReasons; also torchesPlaced: walks are lit like move_to's). find category=ore / category=block gives a tile. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | yes |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |
| `max` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1, ≤ 200 |  | How many tiles at most; default all of an ore vein, 20 of other blocks |
| `torches` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Light the walk: place torches from the inventory in the dark (underground or in a dug tunnel, about every 10 tiles), default true |

### chop_tree

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Chop down a tree with the best axe and collect the wood. Give the trunk's x,y, or omit both for the nearest visible tree that may be chopped: trees near spawn or in NPC houses (protected) and trees whose trunk base isn't visible are skipped (the reply says how many: skipped, skippedReasons), and if the chosen tree can't be reached it moves on to the next nearest (up to 3 trees; the report names the unreachable ones). Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

### blast

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Blow up the block at x,y with a thrown explosive from your inventory — the only way the AI uses explosives (use_item, attack and auto-defend never do). Use it for rock your pickaxe can't break: the Ebonstone / Crimstone around a Shadow Orb / Crimson Heart (pick power 65), or other hard rock. Default explosive: the smallest blast that works, sticky first (Sticky Bomb, Bomb, Sticky Dynamite, Dynamite; Bomb/Sticky Bomb: radius 4 tiles, 3 s fuse; Dynamite: radius 7, 5 s; bouncy variants aren't supported). Before throwing it checks the real tiles within the blast radius + 2 tiles of both the target and the predicted landing spot and refuses (protected_tile) if anything there is furniture, a chest, door, bed or crafting station, inside an NPC house or the spawn area, a Life Crystal / Life Fruit / sword in stone (collect it first), or a Shadow Orb / Crimson Heart without allow_orb (and the 3rd orb without allow_boss_summon, like collect). Altars and other explosion-proof blocks are fine; pots are fine too: the blast breaks them (listed in expectedDestroyed as 'Pot') and their loot is picked up with the other drops. Explosives hurt you: it walks to a spot outside the damage area + a margin with a predicted throw (real throw speed and gravity, only through tiles you can see) that explodes at the target, throws with real controls, stays clear (backs off if it rolls close) until it explodes, retries once if the target survived, then picks up the drops. Auto-defend can't interrupt from the throw to the explosion. A buried target (e.g. an orb deep in rock) is refused with the closest reachable spot: blast the exposed rock nearest to you first (a block next to open space you can see) and work inward, a layer per blast. Also refused when no safe spot to stand exists (a cramped cave: Dynamite needs ~10 tiles of room). Throwing spots the pathfinder proves unreachable are skipped; a spot whose walk fails is remembered for 5 minutes (it and its neighbours are not picked again) and the next best spot is tried. Reply: {item, stand, predictedExplosion, radius, fuseSeconds, expectedDestroyed: {count, byName, tiles, unseen, wallsInRadius, orbs}} — blocks and background walls in the radius are lost. When the task succeeds, report.result is {item, x, y, target, targetDestroyed, blasts, destroyed, destroyedByName, pickedUp: [{name, count}]}. Inventory full: drops that don't fit (all 50 main slots taken, nothing to stack onto; see freeSlots in get_state / get_inventory) stay on the ground, and the task's reason ends with "inventory full: &lt;item> at (x,y) not picked up — drop/trash something (e.g. Ebonstone Block 250) with drop_item and pick_up_items again" (plus an inventory_full event per item). set_reflexes trash_when_full makes room for valuables automatically.  Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

### build_house

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Build a valid town-NPC house (Merchant, Nurse, Demolitionist, Arms Dealer… need one each) with real placement: frame of blocks (floor, walls, ceiling), a door in one side wall, background walls on every inside tile, then a table (or work bench), a chair and a torch. x,y = the bottom-left tile of the frame (floor row); omit both to pick the best visible spot within 30 tiles on ordinary uneven ground, scored by distance and work: ground under at least a third of the floor, floor gaps up to 4 deep get blocks placed over them, natural bumps (dirt/grass/stone, outside protected areas) up to 2 tiles above the floor inside the house or in the door spot are mined first, open air above that (cuttable plants count as air), no trees or natural background walls, room to stand outside the door (2 wide, 3 high, on ground). Your own platforms in the way are handled: unprotected platforms inside the house or in the doorway are mined, ones in the frame are mined and replaced by blocks (a door needs solid blocks above and below; platforms don't count); protected ones (spawn area, holding something up) reject the spot. When no spot is found the error lists the top 3 rejection reasons with counts and an example each. With x,y the same bump mining applies and dips are built over; without door, the door goes on a side with room to stand outside, the side facing you first. Never builds in front of an existing door: a house must leave at least 2 free columns before a neighbouring door (two houses with 1 tile between them make one unreachable). Half blocks and slopes in the frame are hammered flat with your hammer (furniture and doors can't stand on them). Default size 10x6 outer (frame included): vanilla's minimum of 60 tiles; height at most 7 so the ceiling stays in reach. The reply lists frameBlocks, floorGapsToFill, mineFirst, platformsReplaced, flatten, workBenchAt and craftAtBench. Materials come from your inventory: blocks for the frame (Wood first, then other wood, Stone, bricks, Dirt…; existing blocks in the frame's place are kept), owned doors/tables/chairs/torches/house walls first. What is missing is crafted first when possible from any wood you have (Wood, Boreal Wood, Rich Mahogany, Ebonwood, Shadewood, Palm Wood, Pearlwood, Ash Wood: e.g. Ebonwood Door 6, Ebonwood Chair 4, Ebonwood Table 8, Ebonwood Wall 4 per wood, each item from the wood you have most of; Dirt Wall/Stone Wall 4 per block) at a Work Bench; Torch from Gel + any wood needs no station. No Work Bench in range: it places one itself beside the house (one from your inventory, else crafted from 10 wood) as the first step, walks next to it and crafts the rest there (with only the table missing it just crafts a Work Bench as the table). If anything is short it fails up front with missing_item listing exact counts and where to get them; a site that isn't clear fails with bad_params naming the tile (tree: chop_tree it or pick another spot). The player stands inside while building and walks out through the door at the end (move_to opens/closes doors). Then vanilla's housing query runs: succeeded = valid house; failed = built but vanilla's reason (e.g. missing walls). report.result: {x, y, width, height, door, valid, reason?, placed {work bench, frame block, flattened block, door, background wall, table, chair, torch}, skipped, skippedReasons, exitedThroughDoor, housing}. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | no |  |  | Left column of the house frame; omit x and y to find a spot automatically |
| `y` | `integer` | no |  |  | Floor row of the house frame (its bottom row) |
| `width` | `integer` | no | ≥ 8, ≤ 30 |  | Outer width incl. frame, default 10 |
| `height` | `integer` | no | ≥ 5, ≤ 7 |  | Outer height incl. frame, default 6 |
| `door` | `"left" \| "right"` | no |  |  | Side wall for the door; default a side with room to stand outside (2 wide, 3 high), the one facing the player first |

## Combat and reflexes

### attack

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

YOU choose the weapon, ammo and strategy (get_inventory shows damage, useTime, ammoType; get_entities shows the enemy's defense): pass weapon (item name or slot), optionally ammo and strategy. The mod then only does what must happen within a second: aiming, dodging, stepping. Omitting weapon/strategy is a convenience (auto: highest damage-per-second after the target's defense, by weapon style), not a plan; in a real boss fight auto once switched to a useless Wand of Sparking. If the chosen weapon becomes unusable (gone, out of ammo/mana) it falls back to the best alternative and reports it (a weapon_switch event, a recent event and result.switches) and switches back once it works again; fallback: false stops the task with the reason instead. The chosen ammo is moved to the front of the ammo slots (vanilla fires the first matching stack in ammo slots 54-57, then the inventory) and put back when the task ends; when it runs out the next matching ammo fires (reported), or with fallback: false the task stops. strategy: auto (melee closes in, ranged keeps 8-15 tiles), kite (ranged: keep keep_distance tiles, default 12, and keep running along the ground/arena), hit_and_run (melee: step in, swing, back off), hold (stand your ground; only dodging moves you), flee_and_shoot (ranged: keep moving away, shooting backwards). Dodging predicted contact is always on. Fight hostile enemies: closes in for melee or keeps its distance for ranged/magic (per strategy), and does not trade hits — when an enemy is about to touch you (from its hitbox and velocity) it backs off or jumps, never into a hole or lava, still swinging/shooting (melee becomes hit-and-run). target: an entity id from get_entities, "nearest", "boss" (the nearest boss in sight) or "all" = every visible hostile within radius, nearest first, until none remain (one call clears a group). Below retreat_below of max life with no healing potion available (quick-heal reflex handles the rest) it stops attacking, runs away for up to 3 s and fails with reason "low life". When it finishes, wait_for_task's report.result is {killed, kills: [names], damageTaken, durationS, dodges, retreated, potionsUsed, ammoLeft?, weapon, ammo?, strategy, switches?: [messages]}; progress shows the weapon + ammo in use (marked auto or fallback) and the strategy. Never targets town NPCs or critters. BOSS FIGHTS (the target is a boss, e.g. target "boss"): it never pathfinds and never leaves the arena; with a ranged weapon it kites back and forth across the arena (turning near the ends) shooting with lead aim, and dodges dashes sideways, by jumping, or by dropping through the platform underfoot. Jumping bosses (King Slime): it predicts the landing from the jump, runs out from under it or UNDER it to the other side while it is high (its hitbox is huge), learns its jump rhythm and keeps a stance from which the next jump can be dodged, and avoids being pinned at an arena end; give it a wide flat arena (80+ tiles), progress says CORNERED when little arena is left behind you. The boss is the target: a minion is shot only when it is right next to you, unless kill_minions: true (then any minion about to reach you is shot first). A boss that leaves the screen stays the target: you don't see where it is, so it keeps kiting by the last sighting (carried along its last motion) and shoots again once it is back in view. Ends with killed, or fails with "boss fled" when it despawns alive (e.g. the Eye of Cthulhu at dawn). Boss results add {boss, bossKilled, bossLifeLeftPct (when not killed)}; progress shows boss life %, ammo, potions and dodges. Before a boss: build an arena first (build_platforms: 2-3 rows of platforms 60-100 tiles long, spacing ~5 so you can jump between rows), stand on it, carry a bow + plenty of arrows and healing potions, then attack with heal_below ~0.5 and retreat_below 0 (running away from a flying boss doesn't help). Use wait_for_task with a long timeout (fights take minutes) and check get_state between waits. get_boss_info has summon/strategy facts. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `integer \| "nearest" \| "boss" \| "all"` | yes |  |  | Entity id of a hostile enemy, "nearest", "boss" (nearest living boss) or "all" (clear every visible hostile within radius) |
| `radius` | `number` | no | ≥ 1, ≤ 40 |  | For target "all": search radius in tiles, default 25 |
| `retreat_below` | `number` | no | ≥ 0, &lt; 1 |  | Retreat (and fail with 'low life') below this life fraction when no healing is available; default 0.3, 0 = never |
| `heal_below` | `number` | no | ≥ 0, &lt; 1 |  | Quick-heal below this life fraction while this attack runs (only raises the set_reflexes threshold), e.g. 0.5 for a boss |
| `arena` | `{x1: integer, x2: integer}` | no |  |  | Boss fights: the tile columns to stay within (6-400 wide). Default: the walkable ground/platform span around you, up to 50 tiles each way |
| `kill_minions` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Boss fights: shoot any minion about to reach you before the boss (default false: the boss first, minions only when right next to you) |
| `weapon` | `string \| integer` | no | string: non-empty; integer: ≥ 0, ≤ 57 |  | The weapon to fight with: item name or inventory slot 0-57 (get_inventory). Used exactly; omitted or "auto" = the mod picks (convenience only) |
| `ammo` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Ammo item name to fire first (must fit the weapon's ammoType, e.g. Flaming Arrow for a bow); omitted = vanilla's ammo slot order |
| `strategy` | `"auto" \| "kite" \| "hit_and_run" \| "hold" \| "flee_and_shoot"` | no |  |  | How to move: auto (default), kite and flee_and_shoot need a ranged/magic weapon, hit_and_run a melee one, hold any |
| `keep_distance` | `number` | no | ≥ 3, ≤ 30 |  | kite / flee_and_shoot: distance to keep in tiles, default 12 |
| `fallback` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Default true: if the chosen weapon/ammo becomes unusable, use the best alternative (reported). false = stop the task instead |

### set_reflexes

Kind: **instant action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Configure automatic behaviour while you drive: auto_defend (hit hostile enemies in reach, or that just hit you, while idle, waiting, moving, exploring, chopping, mining, placing, picking up or walking to an NPC: the task pauses and resumes after the fight; attack and an item use already under way keep the controls), quick_heal_threshold (quick-heal below this life fraction), pause_when_idle (singleplayer: pause the game while no task runs so you can think), weapon / ammo (what auto-defend fights with; "auto" = the best weapon by damage per second and vanilla's ammo order, the default; a chosen weapon that becomes unusable falls back to the best other one, with a weapon_switch event, and comes back once usable), platform_reserve (platforms every walk — move_to and the walks of mine, collect, explore_caves … — keeps for later descents unless no route fits without them; default 20, 0 = use all), trash_when_full (junk item names, default [] = never: when a valuable item — coins, potions, ores, bars, gems, Life Crystal/Fruit, Mana Crystal, Fallen Star, anything above white rarity such as boss drops — can't be picked up because the inventory is full, one stack of a listed item, earliest in the list first and smallest stack first, never favorited, goes to the trash slot (gone for good) so it fits; at most 5 per task, each with a reflex {kind: "auto_trash"} event; e.g. ["Ebonstone Block", "Dirt Block", "Stone Block", "Mud Block"]; valuable names are refused). Omitted fields keep their value; returns the current settings. Instant action (no task). Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_defend` | `boolean` | no |  |  |  |
| `quick_heal_threshold` | `number` | no | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |  | Life fraction 0..1, e.g. 0.35 |
| `pause_when_idle` | `boolean` | no |  |  |  |
| `weapon` | `string \| integer` | no | string: non-empty; integer: ≥ 0, ≤ 57 |  | Auto-defend weapon: item name or inventory slot 0-57, or "auto" |
| `ammo` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Auto-defend ammo item name (must fit the weapon), or "auto" |
| `platform_reserve` | `integer` | no | ≥ 0, ≤ 9999 |  | Platforms walks keep for descents, default 20 |
| `trash_when_full` | `string[]` | no |  |  | Junk to trash when a valuable drop does not fit, e.g. ["Ebonstone Block", "Dirt Block"]; [] = never (default) |

## NPCs and shops

### talk_to_npc

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Walk within talk range of a visible town NPC and open its chat. Pick the NPC by entity_id or by name (personal name like 'Demetrius' or profession like 'Arms Dealer', case-insensitive; the nearest visible match). Talk range is vanilla's (about 5 tiles across and 4 up/down from your centre) and works through walls: the walk goes to the nearest reachable spot within range, e.g. outside the NPC's house when its door is shut off. Fails with a hint if no such spot is reachable (wait for the NPC to come outside, or build a way/platform). When the task succeeds, wait_for_task's report.result is {name, chat, shop?: [{name, price}]} (shop only if the NPC sells things; price after happiness discounts, e.g. '1 gold 50 silver'). Use buy to purchase. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity_id` | `integer` | no |  |  | Town NPC id from get_entities |
| `name` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Instead of entity_id: the NPC's name or profession, e.g. 'Demetrius' or 'Arms Dealer' |

### buy

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Buy `count` of an item from a visible town NPC's shop with your own coins: walks within talk range of the NPC (as talk_to_npc: through walls, from the nearest reachable spot), opens its shop, buys through the game's normal shop purchase (price includes happiness and discounts), then closes the shop. All of the NPC's shops are searched. Stops early if money or inventory space runs out (still succeeds if at least one was bought). report.result: {npc, item, bought, requested, spent, stopped}. Use talk_to_npc first to see the shop and prices. Selling is not supported. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity_id` | `integer` | no |  |  | Town NPC id from get_entities |
| `name` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Instead of entity_id: the NPC's name or profession, e.g. 'Merchant' |
| `item` | `string` | yes | non-empty |  | Item name as the shop lists it (case-insensitive) |
| `count` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1, ≤ 999 |  | How many, default 1 |

## Chests and beds

### open_chest

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Walk within reach of a chest (or dresser, piggy bank, safe, defender's forge, void vault, modded container) and open it like a right-click. Give any tile of it as x,y, or omit both for the nearest visible one you can open. When the task succeeds, wait_for_task's report.result is {x, y, name, items: [{slot, name, stack}]} — contents are only visible once opened. The chest stays open (get_state shows openChest) for chest_deposit / chest_withdraw until close_chest, another task starts, you walk out of reach (vanilla closes it) or control goes back to the user. Fails on locked chests ('locked': keys are never used automatically), trapped Dead Man's Chests ('rigged') and chests another player has open ('in_use'). Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |

### chest_deposit

Kind: **instant action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Put items into the open chest. Exactly one of: item (+ optional count, default the whole amount; like shift-clicking stacks into the chest, fills partial stacks first; favorited items are never moved), all: true (vanilla 'Deposit All': main inventory and coins, never the hotbar or favorites), quick_stack: true (vanilla 'Quick Stack': only items the chest already holds). Returns {moved: [{name, count}], chest: {x, y, name}, items: [{slot, name, stack}]}; what doesn't fit stays in the inventory (error chest_full if nothing fit). Instant action (no task). Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Item name (case-insensitive) |
| `count` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1 |  | How many, default all of them (only with item) |
| `all` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Deposit All |
| `quick_stack` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Quick Stack onto matching stacks |

### chest_withdraw

Kind: **instant action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Take items out of the open chest into the inventory. Exactly one of: item (+ optional count, default all of it) or all: true (vanilla 'Loot All'). Items go in the way vanilla picks things up (stacking onto existing stacks first); whatever doesn't fit stays in the chest — nothing is ever dropped or deleted (error inventory_full if nothing fit). Returns {moved: [{name, count}], chest, items} like chest_deposit. Instant action (no task). Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | `string` | no | non-empty |  | Item name (case-insensitive) |
| `count` | `integer` | no | ≥ 1 |  | How many, default all of them (only with item) |
| `all` | `boolean` | no |  |  | Loot All |

### close_chest

Kind: **instant action** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Close the open chest (and the inventory, if opening the chest opened it). Returns {closed, chest}; closed is false if none was open. Instant action (no task). Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

Parameters: none.

### loot_chest

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

open_chest + chest_withdraw all + close_chest in one: walks to the chest, opens it like a right-click, presses vanilla 'Loot All' and closes it. Give any tile of it, or omit both for the nearest visible chest you can open. Whatever doesn't fit stays in the chest (nothing is dropped). Locked chests (e.g. dungeon 'Locked Gold Chest': keys are never used automatically), trapped Dead Man's Chests and chests in use are refused. When the task succeeds, report.result is {x, y, name, looted: [{name, count}], left: [{slot, name, stack}]}. Use open_chest instead to see the contents and take only some items. Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |

### use_bed

Kind: **async task** · annotations: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false

Walk to a bed and set your spawn point there, like right-clicking the bed's foot (vanilla rules: the bed must be in valid housing and not obstructed). Give any tile of the bed as x,y, or omit both for the nearest visible bed. When the task succeeds, report.result is {spawnX, spawnY, message}; on failure the reason is vanilla's (e.g. obstructed, room too small, not valid housing). Coordinates are absolute tiles, y grows downward; player position = feet-left tile of its 2x3 body. Starts an async task and returns immediately: follow with wait_for_task (or get_task). Replaces any running task. Fails with user_has_control unless the user pressed Insert to hand over control.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Range | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile x |
| `y` | `integer` | no |  |  | Absolute tile y (grows downward) |

## Prompts

User-invoked templates (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`); Claude Code shows them as `/mcp__terraria__<name>`. The text below is what `prompts/get` returns, with each argument shown as `<name>`.

### prompt: play

**Play toward a goal**: Play the character toward a goal with the standard loop, fair-play rules and control etiquette.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `goal` | yes | What to achieve, e.g. "beat the Eye of Cthulhu" or "get 20 Iron Bars" |
| `time_budget` | no | Optional limit, e.g. "20 minutes" or "one in-game night" |

```text
Play my Terraria character toward this goal: <goal>. Time budget: <time_budget>; stop and report when it is used up.

- Fair play, always: use only what the tools show (fair vision; '?' on get_map is unknown), real controls and vanilla reach; no teleporting, no item spawning, no guessing off-screen positions.
- Control: call request_control before acting. If the user presses Insert (a control_changed event with driver 'user', or user_has_control errors) or request_control is refused, stop at once, don't retry, and ask the user.
- Loop: get_state (position, life, time, bosses, lastDeaths, events) -> get_map / find / get_entities / get_inventory as needed -> one action -> wait_for_task (raise timeout_s for long tasks; on timed_out call it again or cancel_task) -> read report.status/reason and the events (took_damage, player_died, weapon_switch, inventory_full) -> repeat. A new task cancels the running one, so finish or cancel before starting the next.
- Plan only the next step toward the goal; plan the one after that once it is done.
- You decide weapon, ammo and strategy (attack weapon/ammo/strategy, set_reflexes); the mod only does sub-second control.
- Safety: carry healing potions, set_reflexes quick_heal_threshold, keep torches and platforms; at night or low life head for shelter.
- After a death (player_died event, or a new lastDeaths entry), handle it like the after_death prompt before continuing.
- When a task fails, read its reason and change the approach instead of repeating the same call.
- Report progress briefly every few steps, and stop with a summary when the goal is reached or blocked.
```

### prompt: prepare_boss

**Prepare and fight a boss**: Checklist to get ready for a boss (gear, potions, arena, summon) and then fight it with attack.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `boss` | yes | Boss name, e.g. "Eye of Cthulhu" or "King Slime" |

```text
Prepare for <boss> and fight it when ready. Fair play, always: use only what the tools show (fair vision; '?' on get_map is unknown), real controls and vanilla reach; no teleporting, no item spawning, no guessing off-screen positions. Control: call request_control before acting. If the user presses Insert (a control_changed event with driver 'user', or user_has_control errors) or request_control is refused, stop at once, don't retry, and ask the user.

1. get_boss_info boss "<boss>": summon item and recipe, when it can be summoned, stats, tips, defeated. It covers Eye of Cthulhu and King Slime; for other bosses use your own knowledge of vanilla 1.4.4 Classic.
2. get_state and get_inventory: life, defense, armor, weapons (damage, useTime, ammoType), ammo, potions, coins. List what is missing and gather or craft it first, one task at a time (craft with_intermediates).
3. Gear: the best armor equipped (equip), a ranged weapon with plenty of ammo (hundreds of arrows) or a strong melee weapon, healing potions (Lesser Healing Potions at least), and buff potions if you have them.
4. Arena: a flat, open space near the summon spot. build_platforms 2-3 rows 60-100 tiles long with spacing ~5 so you can jump between rows; 80+ tiles wide and flat for King Slime. Stand on it before summoning.
5. Timing: check get_state time (e.g. the Eye of Cthulhu is summoned at night and flees at dawn).
6. Just before: drink buffs with use_item (queue several, then one wait_for_task), select the weapon.
7. Summon with use_item, then attack target "boss" with YOUR choice of weapon, ammo and strategy (e.g. kite for a bow), heal_below ~0.5, retreat_below 0, and arena {x1, x2} = the arena span.
8. wait_for_task with timeout_s 120-300, check get_state (boss life %) between waits; adjust weapon/strategy with a new attack if it goes badly. On death, follow the after_death prompt.
9. After the kill: pick_up_items for the drops, then report the result and suggest the next boss.
```

### prompt: after_death

**Recover after a death**: Read what killed the player, recover dropped coins/items fairly and adjust the plan before retrying.

Arguments: none.

```text
The character died. Recover and adjust before trying again. Fair play, always: use only what the tools show (fair vision; '?' on get_map is unknown), real controls and vanilla reach; no teleporting, no item spawning, no guessing off-screen positions. Control: call request_control before acting. If the user presses Insert (a control_changed event with driver 'user', or user_has_control errors) or request_control is refused, stop at once, don't retry, and ask the user.

1. get_state: lastDeaths[0] (text, killer, x, y, secondsAgo), current position (the spawn point), life, and the events before the death (took_damage sources, reflex quick_heal, weapon_switch).
2. Explain briefly why it happened: which enemy or hazard, low life without potions, cornered, fell, drowned, wrong weapon or ammo ran out.
3. Recover: in Classic mode about half your coins drop where you died (other items too in Mediumcore). Walk back with move_to to the death x,y if the way is safe, then pick_up_items; dropped items despawn after a while.
4. Adjust the plan: better armor or weapon, more potions, a higher quick_heal_threshold or heal_below, a different strategy or arena, fighting in daylight, or skip the danger.
5. Say what you will change, then continue with the next step.
```
